description: The client side of Envoy Gateway: connections by protocol, requests in flight, cancellations, timeouts, TLS and compression.

panels.title: Timed out
panels.description: Requests closed by a header, idle or duration timeout.

panels.title: Cancelled
panels.description: Requests clients abandoned mid-response: skipped segments, closed tabs. Normal in moderation.

panels.title: Reuse
panels.description: Requests each client connection carried on average. Higher means fewer handshakes.

panels.title: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3
panels.description: Requests that arrived over a multiplexed protocol.

panels.title: Compression
panels.description: Bytes compression removed from compressible responses.

panels.title: New connections
panels.description: Client connections opened in the selected range; each one cost a handshake.

panels.title: Requests in flight
panels.description: Requests open at each moment. WebSockets and streams stay open and set the floor.

panels.title: Cancelled and failed requests per hour
panels.description: Cancelled: client left. Reset: stream cut, mostly by a backend or WebSocket close. Timeouts and protocol errors are real failures.

panels.title: Open connections by protocol
panels.description: Client connections open at each moment, by HTTP version.

panels.title: New connections per hour
panels.description: Each new connection costs a TLS or QUIC handshake. HTTP/1.1 clients reconnect the most.

panels.title: Client connection lifetime
panels.description: How long closed client connections stayed open. Short lives mean clients reconnect instead of reusing.

panels.title: Client connection closes per hour
panels.description: Closed by client is normal. Closed by Envoy: idle, drained or asked to close. Cut: closed with requests still open.

panels.title: TLS
panels.description: Days until the served certificate expires (short-lived certs renew with about two left), then handshakes in the range.

panels.title: Requests answered by Envoy per hour
panels.description: Requests Envoy answered without a backend: redirects, fixed responses from route config, unknown hosts or paths, refused WebSockets.

panels.title: Bytes buffered for clients
panels.description: Bytes waiting in client connections: to reach slow clients (up) or to reach backends (down).

panels.title: Compression per hour
panels.description: Compressible response bytes: sent (blue) and saved by compression (gray).

panels.description: Connections or requests refused by a protection: connection caps, overload, size limits, flood guards. Expect none.
